reviews.comment: I think I was actually the only one in this class who truly took notes on the lectures. This class is easy and you don't have to care, but Dr. Wang really is still a great teacher if you listen and follow along. He explained difficult concepts very simply and clearly. Calc 3 with a 1 on difficulty, I mean nobody else could do that. Take him!

Weekly homeworks, dont take very long. Posts all lecture notes, dont need to buy a textbook. Okay lecturer, heavy accent and its his second semester as a professor. Helpful office hours. Do the homeworks and take the practice exams and you will get an A. Overall not difficult and if you do the work you will get the A. Helpful in office hours.

He makes the class extremely easy since the practice exams are copy paste what you'll see on the real exams. However, he wasn't a great lecturer (I think he's a new professor), and I pretty much learned everything from doing the homework. It's very simple to earn an A in this class if you turn in your homework on time and do the practice exams.

OK lectures, but lecture notes are posted on Canvas and are very easy to follow, so attendance isn't mandatory. 
Doesn't make you buy the textbook.
Posts sample exams that are very very similar to the actual exam. So exams are incredibly easy. 
He's a very nice person; office hours were very helpful.

Doesn't make you buy the textbook for his class, only one homework assignment per week, notes are helpful and concise and posted on Canvas before every lecture, test reviews and practice exams honestly carry. His class has an amazing setup and I wish all my classes were like this. Beware the final is 35% of your grade.

The lectures are pretty monotonous and boring, with the professor barely being able to understand your questions; however, the tests are straight off of a review guide, which makes the class manageable even without the lectures.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He releases study guides for the exams that are the exact same question types as the real exams including the final. There were 2 exam, 1 final, and 13 homeworks. I think this was his first semester teaching, but I think he will be a great professor in the future.

There's 13 HW's (drop lowest), 2 Midterms, & a final. Lectures are straight from the posted notes w/ nothing added, & his accent makes it hard to understand sometimes anyway. Test's are straight from the given reviews w/ numbers changed. Go through the notes & you're fine, relatively easy class as long as you don't get behind.
